items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: And I picked up a fellow by the name of Bill Moore, who was a mulatto, and really was the first Negro musician to play in a white band

ctx.x: This was about ten years after the original Dixieland jazz band played New York, or seven or eight years anyway. And by this time, the boys had begun to either get other influences or show a great deal of originality. They were using the original New Orleans jazz as a background, but they were beginning to show a little independence on phrasing.

Yes, they were evolving. They were evolving. Don't forget the old stuff was kind of raw, and very few people could play it, you know? Certainly the New Yorkers. Yes. And I picked up a fellow by the name of Bill Moore, who was a mulatto, and really was the first Negro musician to play in a white band, a big white swing band. Benny Goodman claims that prestige, but it's not so.
The Rams beat it by ten years. Well, I mentioned Durante, and Durante had baquet, so there's another case of a mixed band.
